issues.legal_issue: The statutory terms for estate holders include incorporated companies that own estates when the legislation’s context and purpose do not exclude them.
material_facts: The appellants were incorporated companies that owned estates or parts of estates.
The legislation defined estate holders using the word “person” and included a person who owned an estate or part of one.
The legislation’s object was to reform land distribution by acquiring estates, and a company could own and hold property.
The companies challenged notifications declaring their estates vested in the State.
issues.conclusion: The word “person” in the definitions of proprietor and tenure-holder includes incorporated companies, so the legislation applies to companies owning estates.
issues.legal_principle: The Bihar General Clauses Act, section 4(40), provides that “person” includes a company unless there is something repugnant in the subject or context. Sections 2(o) and 2(r) of the Bihar Land Reforms Act define “proprietor” and “tenure-holder,” and section 3 authorizes vesting notifications. The Court held that the definitions’ ownership language covers companies and that including companies advances the Act’s purpose of land-distribution reform, as explained in State of Bihar v. Kameshwar Singh, [1952] SCR 889, at 941. Pharmaceutical Society v. London and Provincial Supply Association, Ltd. (1880) 5 App. Cas. 857 was distinguished because the object and context of that legislation made corporate inclusion repugnant. The Court also rejected the arguments based on winding-up provisions and section 41, noting that company officers or agents could comply with relevant requirements.

rule.if: appeal_from_writ_challenge and company_owns_estate and law_targets_estate_ownership and definition_uses_person_for_owner and no_contextual_incompatibility

predicates.appeal_from_writ_challenge: A party appeals after a court dismisses a writ challenge to a notification taking an estate into state ownership.
predicates.company_owns_estate: An incorporated company owns an estate or part of an estate.
predicates.law_targets_estate_ownership: The legislation is directed at acquiring estates to reform land distribution.
predicates.definition_uses_person_for_owner: The legislation defines an estate holder by reference to a person who owns or holds an estate.
predicates.no_contextual_incompatibility: The subject and context of the legislation do not make it inappropriate to treat a company as a person.

issues.definition: When a company owns an estate, a land-reform law defines an estate holder by reference to a person, and the law’s context does not exclude companies, the company is covered by the definition in an appeal from a writ challenge to the taking of the estate.

issues.legal_issue: A notification taking the part of an estate within a state is not invalid merely because the estate, its revenue arrangements, or its leases extend beyond that state and require apportionment.
material_facts: One company owned estates situated both within and outside the state where the land-reform law operated.
The company paid a single government revenue and had leases covering land on both sides of the state boundary.
The notification covered only the part of the estate situated within the state.
The company argued that the estate could not be severed and that taking only part would make revenue and rent collection difficult.
issues.conclusion: The notification covering the part of the estate within the state was valid; the need to apportion revenue and rent did not affect its validity.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the matter as one of apportioning revenue and rent. The practical need for apportionment did not invalidate a notification taking the portion of an estate situated within the state.

rule.if: appeal_from_writ_challenge and estate_spans_state_boundary and notification_covers_local_part and revenue_or_rent_requires_apportionment

predicates.appeal_from_writ_challenge: A party appeals after a court dismisses a writ challenge to a notification taking an estate into state ownership.
predicates.estate_spans_state_boundary: An estate includes land situated within and outside the state whose law provides for the taking.
predicates.notification_covers_local_part: The notification takes only the portion of the estate situated within that state.
predicates.revenue_or_rent_requires_apportionment: The estate’s revenue or rent arrangements cover land both within and outside the state and therefore require apportionment.

issues.definition: When an estate spans a state boundary, a notification takes only its local portion, and revenue or rent must be apportioned, the notification remains valid in an appeal from a writ challenge.
